description: Health and Physical Education Y7-8 width tiers — 19 descriptors across Personal, Social and Community Health and Movement and Physical Activity strands. ACARA v9.
subject: Health and Physical Education

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest honest encounter with the descriptor's command term. For capability descriptors (analyse, design, investigate, propose): minimum is a single focused context in which the skill is genuinely exercised. For understanding descriptors (examine, explain): minimum involves at least one real scenario or example through which the concept is engaged.
width_notes.typical_width: The full scope of the descriptor as ACARA intended it, grounded in the most common elaboration cases. A class that has engaged with the typical range has met the descriptor's spirit.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions that add new contexts, community settings, cultural perspectives or application domains — not harder versions of the same task. First Nations elaborations are always included in wider where present.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as source data, not a checklist. Verbatim elaborations preserved per descriptor. Some elaborations represent sub-steps of the same activity and are treated as one item.

AC9HP8M01.minimum_width: Use feedback from one source (teacher or peer) to identify and make at least one specific refinement to a movement skill in a single game or physical activity context.
AC9HP8M01.typical_width: Analyse, refine and transfer movement skills across multiple movement types (games, dance, aquatics, obstacle/outdoor contexts) using feedback from teachers, peers, video or self-reflection to make targeted adjustments.
wider: Apply feedback-to-refinement cycles in an outdoor or nature-based movement context (e.g. navigation, ropes course, trail running) where terrain variability requires continuous skill adaptation
Compare how feedback is interpreted and applied differently in individual versus team movement contexts, such as swimming versus invasion games
Investigate how elite athletes use video analysis and coaching feedback loops to refine technique, then apply a simplified version of this approach to their own skill development
elaborations: implementing feedback from a teacher to refine how they move within the playing or performance space
using feedback from teammates in a game to know when to travel, mark or intercept to achieve and retain possession
using feedback from a peer coach to adapt movement sequences to create, use and defend space in invasion, net/court, striking and fielding, and target games
refining a range of swimming strokes using feedback from a teacher, peers or video resources
using feedback from others to refine the composition of a group dance sequence
using feedback from others to safely and efficiently travel around, over, up, under and through natural or built obstacles

AC9HP8M02.minimum_width: Design a movement strategy for one specific scenario and demonstrate it, explaining one intended improvement to the movement outcome.
AC9HP8M02.typical_width: Design and demonstrate movement strategies across a range of scenarios (game contexts, balance sequences, tactical situations); predict and explain the effect of changes in strategy on movement outcomes; revisit successful strategies and adapt them to new challenges.
wider: Design movement strategies for non-traditional or student-invented game contexts, evaluating how the same principles (space, flow, balance) generalise across very different movement forms
Investigate how professional coaching teams design game strategies using data and spatial analysis, then translate a simplified version to a class game context
Explore how the principles of static and dynamic balance underlying gymnastics and yoga also appear in team sport movement sequences, designing a task that deliberately links them
elaborations: developing and implementing appropriate strategies for selected movement scenarios
selecting strategies that have been successful previously and applying the most appropriate ones when solving new movement challenges
exploring similarities between the bases of support and flow of movements when performing different movement sequences that require static and dynamic balance
predicting the effectiveness of changes in tactics or strategies on scoring opportunities and suggesting reasons for any unexpected results

AC9HP8M03.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least one movement concept (effort, space, time, objects or people) and explain how manipulating it changes a movement outcome in one activity.
AC9HP8M03.typical_width: Demonstrate and explain how multiple movement concepts (effort, space, time, objects and people) can be manipulated across a range of movement forms, including game contexts, rhythmic sequences and performance designs; explain links between biomechanical concepts (angle of release, take-off, landing) and movement outcomes.
wider: Analyse and design a rhythmic or artistic movement sequence (e.g. dance, gymnastics) that deliberately uses manipulation of space, flow and relationships to communicate an idea or emotion to an audience

Investigate how movement concepts apply in adaptive or modified sport contexts, and design a movement task that accommodates a range of physical abilities while maintaining the integrity of the movement concept

Explore how movement concepts used in sport and physical activity connect to traditional First Nations Australian movement forms, examining similarities and differences in how effort, space and relationships are used
elaborations: performing a range of movements and analysing technique based on understanding of effort in relation to take-off, body position and landing
demonstrating an understanding of how to adjust the angle of release of an object and how this will affect the height and distance of flight
creating, performing and appraising rhythmic movement sequences that demonstrate variations in flow of movements, use of space and relationships to other performers
designing and refining performances to demonstrate how to manipulate space and relationships between players in the space to achieve successful movement outcomes

AC9HP8M04.minimum_width: Participate in at least one physical activity designed to improve a fitness component and describe one effect of that participation on health, fitness or wellbeing.
AC9HP8M04.typical_width: Participate in a range of physical activities targeting different fitness components and wellbeing dimensions; investigate the effects of regular participation using evidence (including digital tools or health guidelines); design a realistic personal activity program connected to individual goals.
wider: Research and participate in unfamiliar activity forms (yoga, mindfulness, HIIT, martial arts) and compare how each addresses different dimensions of health and wellbeing
Design a fitness program for a specific health goal using digital tracking tools and evaluate its effectiveness over a period of weeks against self-set benchmarks

Investigate how access to fitness and wellbeing activities varies across different community contexts (e.g. rural vs urban, different socioeconomic settings) and the implications for equity in health outcomes
elaborations: using digital tools to design personal physical activity programs that support regular participation and meet their individual health, wellbeing and fitness goals
designing and performing a fitness circuit they could implement at home (with minimal equipment) that improves one or more fitness components
researching and participating in new activities to explore how they can enhance health, fitness and wellbeing, such as yoga, mindfulness meditation, gym classes, HIIT sessions

AC9HP8M05.minimum_width: Participate in one physical activity in a community or outdoor setting and identify one strategy that supports or could increase use of that space.
AC9HP8M05.typical_width: Participate in activities across different community and outdoor settings; evaluate strategies for managing and protecting environments used for physical activity; design physical activity options that reimagine or better utilise community spaces.
wider: Investigate First Nations Australian custodial practices for Country/Place and how these approaches to caring for land and water can inform sustainable management of community physical activity spaces
Research and evaluate minimal-impact outdoor recreation principles and design a code of practice for a specific local outdoor setting used for physical activity
Investigate how urban design and planning decisions affect access to community spaces for physical activity, and propose a redesign of an underutilised local space
elaborations: evaluating different strategies used to manage and protect environments where physical activities take place, such as bushwalking trails, surf beaches, skate parks and sporting fields

investigating different approaches to custodial responsibility for Country/Place used by First Nations Australian communities to support the use of local settings and spaces for physical activity while protecting the environment
designing and evaluating physical activity options that reimagine the use of community spaces to encourage more active lifestyles among their peer group
promoting an understanding of minimal-impact outdoor recreation in the local area

AC9HP8M06.minimum_width: Design one strategy to increase physical activity levels and provide at least one justification for how it would support a health or wellbeing outcome.
AC9HP8M06.typical_width: Design and justify a range of strategies targeting increased physical activity, reduced sedentary behaviour, improved social connection and wellbeing; compare current activity levels to Australia's 24-Hour Movement Guidelines and suggest evidence-based improvements.
wider: Design a physical activity program for a specific peer group (e.g. students who prefer non-competitive activity, or those with mobility considerations) with explicit justification for each design decision
Investigate the relationship between social connection, emotional wellbeing and physical activity, and design a program that explicitly targets both physical and social outcomes simultaneously
Analyse how the 24-Hour Movement Guidelines apply differently across different life stages or contexts and evaluate the assumptions built into the guidelines
elaborations: designing and monitoring a personal physical activity plan that proposes realistic strategies for increasing physical activity levels and reducing sedentary behaviours
investigating which physical activities people engage in to maintain emotional and social wellbeing, and designing a program of activities aimed at increasing social connection and wellbeing

comparing their current physical activity levels, amount of sleep and sedentary activity time with Australia's 24-Hour Movement Guidelines for Children and Young People and suggesting strategies for themselves and others to meet these recommendations

AC9HP8M07.minimum_width: Propose at least one movement strategy for a given situation and evaluate whether it was effective, giving one reason.
AC9HP8M07.typical_width: Propose and evaluate movement strategies across a range of movement situations (games, outdoor/nature activities, movement challenges); justify selections based on factors such as success, context and transferability; test proposed solutions and reflect on outcomes.
wider: Apply propose-and-evaluate cycles to an outdoor or nature-based activity context (orienteering, canoeing, bushwalking) where environmental unpredictability requires ongoing strategy revision
Investigate how transfer of movement learning occurs — examining which skills and strategies from one movement context genuinely transfer to another, and why some do not
Design a movement challenge that requires others to propose and evaluate strategies, and reflect on what the design process revealed about effective strategy selection
elaborations: evaluating factors that enabled them to achieve success in movement activities and justifying how these factors can be transferred to other learning contexts

explaining and justifying the movement strategies selected in response to movement challenges when participating in outdoor or nature-based activities such as rope courses, bushwalking, orienteering or canoeing
putting their movement solutions into action by predicting outcomes and testing the approach proposed to achieve successful movement outcomes

AC9HP8M08.minimum_width: Investigate one modification (to rules, equipment or scoring) in a physical activity and explain how it supports fair play or inclusive participation.
AC9HP8M08.typical_width: Investigate and apply modifications to rules, equipment and scoring systems across a range of physical activities; analyse the benefits and drawbacks of player-officiated games; explore how modifications create fairer and more inclusive participation conditions.
wider: Explore rules, equipment and scoring systems of traditional games of First Nations Australians and investigate how they support skill development, fair play and inclusive participation
Design a modified version of a game from scratch for a specific group with particular participation needs (e.g. mixed ability, mixed age), testing and evaluating the design against inclusion criteria
Research how modified sport programs (e.g. Auslan volleyball, sitting volleyball, bocce) extend participation and compare the design principles used to those applied in classroom game modifications
elaborations: modifying rules, equipment or scoring systems to allow all participants to enjoy success in physical activities
applying and adapting scoring systems in activities to assess movement performances consistently and fairly
analysing the benefits and potential drawbacks of activities where players, rather than an independent official, are responsible for officiating the game
exploring rules, equipment and scoring systems of traditional games of First Nations Australians and investigating how they support skill development and fair and inclusive play

AC9HP8M09.minimum_width: Adopt one leadership or collaboration role in a physical activity and identify one way your actions contributed to the team or group outcome.
AC9HP8M09.typical_width: Practise and apply leadership, collaboration and decision-making across a range of physical activity contexts; adopt varied roles (leader, collaborator, planner); use verbal, physical and situational cues to read and respond to others; reflect on how specific actions shaped outcomes.
wider: Plan and lead a physical activity for a peer group from design through to facilitation, evaluating leadership decisions made at each stage

Investigate how leadership styles differ across different physical activity contexts (competitive team sport vs cooperative challenge vs outdoor recreation) and reflect on which approaches transferred most effectively

Explore how cultural understandings of leadership and collaboration influence group decision-making in physical activities, including examining examples from First Nations Australian community sport contexts
elaborations: adopting roles and responsibilities that support and enhance team cohesion and lead to successful movement outcomes
applying an understanding of verbal, physical and situational cues to identify and appropriately respond to the feelings and motives of others when working in a team or group
reflecting on their role and articulating how the actions they initiated in that role led to the achievement of successful outcomes
undertaking various roles as a leader or collaborator to support the planning of physical activities for their team or peer group

AC9HP8P01.minimum_width: Identify at least one way values or beliefs (personal, family or cultural) influence identity development, and reflect on how this has shaped a sense of self.
AC9HP8P01.typical_width: Analyse how values and beliefs from multiple sources (personal, family, peer, cultural) influence identity development; examine how cultural beliefs about puberty and physical change affect gender, cultural and sexual identities; reflect on how this analysis applies to their own developing sense of identity.
wider: Analyse how naming and mourning protocols in First Nations Australian communities (such as kumanjayi) reflect community values and their impact on identity and belonging
Examine how young Australians of Asian heritage navigate between home cultural values and Australian social norms, and the identity negotiations this involves
Investigate how social media and digital culture create new sites of identity formation, particularly for young people navigating cultural, gender or sexual identity
elaborations: examining how their values and beliefs, as well as those of family and friends, influence the development of identities
analysing how naming of deceased protocols, such as kumanjayi, can impact the identities of other members within First Nations Australian communities
examining how cultural values and beliefs influence the way young people view themselves, including young Australians of Asian heritage
examining how cultural beliefs about the physical changes experienced during puberty can influence gender, cultural and sexual identities

AC9HP8P02.minimum_width: Identify one significant change or transition relevant to their age group and describe one strategy for managing its impact on themselves or others.
AC9HP8P02.typical_width: Analyse the impact of multiple changes and transitions (peer/family relationships, puberty, health transitions, cultural transitions); access and assess support resources; devise coping, communication and problem-solving strategies; examine how ceremonies and cultural transitions mark changes in social standing.
wider: Examine the concept of 'border crossing' and how First Nations Australians navigate transitions between multiple cultural contexts, and the impact on sense of belonging and identity
Research how transition support programs for young people are designed and evaluate their effectiveness in addressing key challenges at developmental transition points
Investigate sexual health information and services available to young people, evaluate their accessibility and relevance, and devise a strategy for how young people could access them confidently
elaborations: investigating the changing nature of peer and family relationships and proposing strategies to manage these changes

accessing and assessing health information and services that support young people to effectively manage changes and transitions as they grow older, including sexual health information about sexually transmitted infections, contraception and safe sexual practices
examining how ceremonies of First Nations Australians involve sharing of cultural knowledge leading to changes in social standing and responsibilities in communities

examining the notion of 'border crossing'; that is, how First Nations Australians live across multiple cultures, and how these transitions can impact on a sense of belonging to culture, family and peer groups
evaluating and practising coping, communication and problem-solving skills to manage changes and emotions associated with puberty and getting older

AC9HP8P03.minimum_width: Examine one example of how gender stereotypes influence roles, decisions or power in a relationship and identify one attribute valued regardless of gender.
AC9HP8P03.typical_width: Examine how gender stereotypes influence roles, decision-making, power and coercion in a range of relationship types (friendships, sexual relationships, family); investigate successful strategies for challenging harmful stereotypes; identify positive character attributes valued across genders.
wider: Analyse intergenerational patterns of gender inequality from texts or scenarios, examining how power imbalances are reproduced across generations and how they can be disrupted
Research campaigns or community initiatives that have been effective in challenging gender stereotypes, evaluating the strategies used and their impact on attitudes and behaviours
Examine how gender stereotypes intersect with cultural or racial expectations, and how young people from diverse backgrounds navigate these intersecting pressures
elaborations: exploring scenarios in texts that demonstrate how gender inequality can arise from intergenerational patterns of inequity and unequal power in relationships
examining how gender roles and stereotypes can influence beliefs and decisions about self, friendships, sexual relationships, sexual behaviour, contraceptive use, substance use and future life plans
identifying those positive character attributes and strengths that are valued regardless of gender
investigating strategies that have been successful in challenging harmful or limiting stereotypes, attitudes or practices

AC9HP8P04.minimum_width: Examine one example of respect, empathy, power or coercion in a relationship context and explain how it affects the quality of that relationship.
AC9HP8P04.typical_width: Examine how respect, empathy, power and coercion operate across a range of relationship types (peer, online, family, intimate); analyse how context (alone, with friends, with family) changes behaviour; identify what constitutes disrespectful, harmful or violent behaviour; propose strategies for addressing racism and discrimination.
wider: Examine strategies for addressing racism towards First Nations Australians, including the role of bystanders in promoting respectful interactions and challenging discrimination in everyday contexts
Investigate how cultural norms and values shape expectations for respectful behaviour, and how students can navigate respectfully across cultural difference in relationships
Analyse scenarios involving online harassment, image-based abuse or grooming and evaluate the strategies available to targets and bystanders for responding effectively
elaborations: analysing how behaviours, actions and responses to situations can change depending on whether they are by themselves, with friends or with family
recognising the impact bullying and harassment can have on relationships, including online relationships
showing respect for cultural norms and sensitivities when building relationships with people from different cultural backgrounds
proposing strategies for addressing racism towards First Nations Australians, including the role of bystanders in promoting respectful interactions and challenging disrespect and discrimination
examining what constitutes disrespectful, harmful or violent behaviour within peer, family and intimate relationships

AC9HP8P05.minimum_width: Investigate one strategy that supports community valuing of diversity and propose one action to promote inclusion.
AC9HP8P05.typical_width: Investigate strategies influencing community valuing of diversity across multiple dimensions (gender, race, sexuality, ability); examine how stereotypes are challenged at local, national and global levels; propose concrete inclusion actions; investigate events that value First Nations Australian contributions.
wider: Investigate events and strategies that value First Nations Australian contributions and strengthen relationships — such as Indigenous rounds in sporting codes or NAIDOC Week — evaluating their effectiveness in shifting community attitudes

Research how cultural practices and beliefs from Asian communities in Australia have been received and integrated over time, examining examples of cultural exchange and persistent barriers to inclusion
Design and evaluate an inclusion campaign targeting a specific form of discrimination (e.g. ableism, homophobia) in a school or community context, drawing on evidence from comparable campaigns
elaborations: investigating how respecting diversity and challenging racism, sexism, ableism and homophobia influence individual and community health and wellbeing
examining values and beliefs about cultural and social issues such as gender, race, violence, sexuality and ability, and how resisting stereotypes can help students be themselves
developing strategies to challenge narrow views of gender, race, violence, sexuality, gender diversity and ability to contribute to inclusive communities
researching how norms, stereotypes and prejudice are challenged in local, national and global contexts
investigating events and strategies that value the contributions of First Nations Australians and strengthen relationships, such as Indigenous rounds in sporting codes and NAIDOC Week

identifying examples of beliefs and cultural practices within, between and across cultural groups, including cultural groups from the Asian region, and describing how they have changed or remained the same over time

AC9HP8P06.minimum_width: Identify one personal, social or cultural factor influencing emotional responses in a given situation and describe one strategy for managing that response.
AC9HP8P06.typical_width: Analyse personal, social and cultural factors influencing emotional responses across a range of situations; consider alternative perspectives and practise empathy; recognise and interpret responses to stress; propose strategies that prevent negative impact on others.
wider: Investigate how cultural backgrounds shape emotional expression and management, examining how different cultural norms create different expectations for emotional responses in the same situation
Explore how social media and digital environments create new emotional pressures for young people, and devise strategies for managing emotional responses in online contexts
Research how emotional self-regulation is developed and supported in therapeutic or community wellbeing contexts, and evaluate which strategies could be applied in everyday settings
elaborations: investigating personal, social and cultural factors that influence the way individuals respond emotionally to different situations and determining the impact these responses could have on others
exploring different viewpoints, practising being empathetic and considering alternative ways to respond in a variety of situations, which take into account how they may affect others
recognising and interpreting emotional responses to stressful situations and proposing strategies for ensuring those responses don't have a negative impact on others

AC9HP8P07.minimum_width: Explain what consent means in at least one relationship context and demonstrate one assertive strategy for seeking, giving or denying consent.
AC9HP8P07.typical_width: Explain and apply assertive, respectful communication skills for seeking, giving and denying consent across relationship contexts (in-person and online); examine the nature of consent in different relationship types; recognise and respond to harmful online content (grooming, image-based abuse).
wider: Investigate how consent communication is complicated by power imbalances, group pressure or digital contexts, and practise strategies that work effectively across these more challenging situations
Research how legal frameworks around consent for young people are designed to protect them, and evaluate how awareness of these frameworks supports safer relationships

Design and role-play scenarios where students practise assertive consent communication in a range of realistic contexts, including digital/online scenarios, and reflect on what made each scenario challenging
elaborations: exploring and refining skills and strategies needed to communicate assertively and respectfully in relationships

understanding and applying online and social protocols to enhance relationships with others and protect their own wellbeing, including recognising and responding to online content that may be harmful for themselves or others (such as grooming or image-based abuse), respectfully communicating needs or concerns to others
examining the nature of consent in different types of relationships, and proposing and practising strategies for seeking, giving and denying consent respectfully

AC9HP8P08.minimum_width: Identify one community resource available to support mental health or safety and explain one protective behaviour strategy for a given scenario.
AC9HP8P08.typical_width: Refine protective behaviours and evaluate community resources across multiple help-seeking domains (mental health, online safety, substance use, bullying); examine how emotions, social supports and cultural norms affect help-seeking; analyse the role of bystanders in ensuring online safety.
wider: Investigate how gender norms and cultural expectations create barriers to help-seeking for different groups of young people, and design strategies that address these barriers
Analyse how online support services (Kidshelpline, eSafety Commissioner) are designed and evaluate their effectiveness for different types of situations young people encounter

Explore help-seeking scenarios involving substance use (alcohol, e-cigarettes, cannabis, inhalants) and collaborate to devise strategies for navigating each situation, including how to support a friend who is using
elaborations: exploring different strategies they can use, and resources or help sites they can access or refer others to, if they are experiencing symptoms of anxiety or depression
examining scenarios to highlight how emotions, dispositions, social supports, and gender and cultural norms can affect a person's willingness to seek help

exploring strategies for dealing with online abuse and bullying when there is an imbalance of power, such as grooming, image-based abuse or negative social interactions, and reporting the situation to appropriate authorities, trusted adults and through online tools
collaborating with peers to suggest strategies they could use if they are being encouraged to use a substance such as alcohol, e-cigarettes, cannabis or inhalants

analysing how bystanders play a role in ensuring online spaces are positive and safe, and examining how support services such as kidshelpline and the eSafety Commissioner can provide support for young people who feel unsafe, bullied or abused online

exploring help-seeking scenarios young people may encounter and sharing strategies for dealing with each situation, including situations linked to substance use, mental health issues, safety and risk-taking, and sexual health

AC9HP8P09.minimum_width: Investigate one media source conveying a health message, evaluate its credibility or reliability, and explain how it might influence a health decision.
AC9HP8P09.typical_width: Investigate how media and influential people (news sites, bloggers, influencers, advertising) impact health attitudes, beliefs and decisions across multiple health domains (food, sexual relationships, mental health, body image); analyse credibility, validity and relevance of sources; apply credible information to health decisions.
wider: Explore health campaigns targeting First Nations Australian young people (e.g. Deadly Choices, Don't Make Smokes Your Story, Yarn Safe) and analyse the messages, strategies and cultural framing used
Analyse how sexual relationship and body image messages are constructed in different media forms and evaluate their potential influence on young people's beliefs and behaviours
Investigate how social media algorithms shape the health information young people encounter, and evaluate what media literacy strategies help them navigate this environment critically
elaborations: analysing the credibility, validity and relevance of health messages conveyed by different sources (including news sites, bloggers, influencers and social media advertising) and applying credible information to health-related decisions
investigating how messages related to food are portrayed in the media and how this may impact decision-making in relation to health and wellbeing

exploring and evaluating the accessibility and reliability of health information sources from the media that target young people in relation to their health, wellbeing, body, sexuality, relationships and other health issues

exploring health campaigns targeting First Nations Australian young people and discussing the messages and strategies used to promote and enhance their health; for example, Deadly Choices, Don't Make Smokes Your Story and Yarn Safe
analysing how messages related to sexual relationships are portrayed in different forms of media and how they may influence the way people act within relationships

AC9HP8P10.minimum_width: Plan and implement one strategy using at least one health resource to enhance health, safety or wellbeing for themselves or others.
AC9HP8P10.typical_width: Plan and implement strategies using a range of health resources across multiple health domains (physical activity, nutrition, mental health, digital wellbeing); evaluate the impact of strategies; investigate preventive health practices; design health promotion activities targeting relevant practices for young people.
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australians have developed complete diets meeting nutritional requirements and used food for medicinal purposes, and examine how this knowledge connects to contemporary nutritional understanding

Examine how different cultural traditions value mind-body-spirit connections to health (e.g. Dadirri from First Nations of the Daly River region, yoga and meditation from the Asian region) and evaluate their relevance to young people's wellbeing
Design and implement a health promotion campaign targeting a specific preventive health practice, evaluating its impact on attitudes or behaviours within the school or local community
elaborations: proposing and implementing actions and behaviours that promote safe participation in physical activities, and evaluating the impact participation can have on their own and others' mood and mental wellbeing
investigating food-serving recommendations from The Australian Guide to Healthy Eating and producing a guide to help students make healthy choices when buying food from the school canteen
researching a variety of snack and lunch options, and evaluating nutritional value, value for money and sustainability to create a weekly menu plan
investigating how First Nations Australians have developed complete diets that meet nutritional requirements, and used and continue to use food for medicinal purposes
examining how different cultures value the contribution of the mind-body-spirit connection to health and wellbeing; for example, Dadirri and yoga and meditation practices from the Asia region
investigating preventive health practices relevant to young people, and designing and implementing health promotion activities targeting these practices
investigating tools and designing routines that help to regulate the use of digital environments and tools and ensure a healthy pattern of use
investigating different approaches and developing personal plans for promoting their own positive mental health and wellbeing, such as mindfulness, relaxation techniques and healthy eating
